Which of the following is a valid way to integrate CSS into a webpage?
explanation: In web development, CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) can be integrated into a webpage in three valid ways: inline, internal, and external. Inline CSS is applied directly to an HTML element using the style attribute. It is useful for applying quick styles to individual elements but is not recommended for larger projects due to poor maintainability. Internal CSS is written within a <style> tag inside the <head> section of an HTML document. This method is suitable for styling single-page websites or small projects where all the styles are contained within the same file. External CSS, on the other hand, involves linking an external .css file to the HTML document using a <link> tag. This is the most scalable and maintainable method, especially for larger websites, as it separates content from presentation and allows styles to be reused across multiple pages. Therefore, all three methods—inline, internal, and external—are valid ways to incorporate CSS into a webpage, making "All of the above" the correct answer.

q: What will be the output of the following code snippet?
explanation: In JavaScript, if you define the same key more than once in an object, the last occurrence of that key overwrites any previous values. So, in the object {first: 20, second: 30, first: 50}, the second first: 50 overwrites the earlier first: 20. As a result, the object becomes {first: 50, second: 30}. There’s no syntax error here. JavaScript allows duplicate keys during object creation, but only the last one is retained.

q: Which of the following is not a difference between HTML and XHTML?
options: Charset in both html and xhtml is “text/html”
Tags and attributes are case-insensitive in HTML but not in XHTML
Special characters must be escaped using character entities in XHTML unlike HTML
Charset in html is “text/html” where as in xhtml it is “application/xml+xhtml”
